title: Restore silently dropped 71 tables across two databases via case-sensitive dump lookup
description:
The mental_healths_large and organ_transplant_large mirrors are missing 34 and
37 tables respectively because restore resolves dump files case-sensitively
while the upstream dump ships lowercase filenames. The data is present locally
and fully recoverable. This is a provisioning defect in this repository, not an
upstream benchmark defect, not a broken Neon restore, and not a reader-grant
problem.

MEASUREMENT

Declared tables come from data/raw/livesqlbench-large-v1/schema/<db>/<db>_schema.txt,
restored counts from config/databases/livesqlbench-large-v1.json verification.table_count.

  mental_healths_large     55 declared, 21 restored, 34 missing
  organ_transplant_large   57 declared, 20 restored, 37 missing

All 16 other databases show zero missing tables.

The missing sets are exactly the scorer_omitted_tables entries recorded for
those two databases: 34 and 37. Case-insensitively, every declared table has a
dump file; 55 of 55 and 57 of 57 resolve. Case-sensitively, 0 of 34 and 0 of 37
of the omitted names resolve, and every one of them has a dump file that differs
only in capitalization.

  omitted 'Facilities'               actual dump file 'facilities.sql'
  omitted 'Patients'                 actual dump file 'patients.sql'
  omitted 'AssessmentBasics'         actual dump file 'assessmentbasics.sql'
  omitted 'Demographics'             actual dump file 'demographics.sql'
  omitted 'HLA_Info'                 actual dump file 'hla_info.sql'
  omitted 'Function_and_Recovery'    actual dump file 'function_and_recovery.sql'

MECHANISM

database_postgres.py restore_database builds each candidate as
dump_root / f"{table}.sql" from restore_order, and for any table listed in
omitted_tables it asserts the candidate does NOT exist, then skips it. Because
the omitted names are CamelCase and the shipped files are lowercase, that
non-existence assertion passes on a case-sensitive filesystem. The missing data
was therefore recorded as an intentional omission rather than raised as a
restore failure. scorer_continues_after_sql_error is also True for both
databases. Both fields were introduced in de7ed6d.

WHY EVERY DOWNSTREAM CHECK PASSED

verification.schema_sha256 and content_sha256 were computed after the truncated
restore, so they fingerprint the truncated state and match it exactly.
readonly_role_verified and external_parity are both True against that same
truncated state. This is why omni-benchmark-2j9 was closed as refuted: its live
parity check was correct about what it compared and could not have detected
this.

IMPACT

- 18 dev-A questions (9 per database) currently unscorable.
- 54 attempts in the completed direct baseline scored gold_statement_error;
  that category was correct, since the benchmark gold references tables that
  were never loaded.
- Both databases' share of the sealed 101, since the split is stratified by
  database. Freeze B must not commit these snapshot identifiers as they stand.
- omni-benchmark-wk0 was drafted assuming these 18 questions were permanently
  unrecoverable. That assumption is now wrong and its option set changes again.

FIX

1. Correct dump-file resolution so a capitalization-only mismatch is an error
   rather than a silent skip. An omitted-table declaration must not be
   satisfiable by a case variant of an existing file.
2. Clear scorer_omitted_tables for both databases and re-derive
   scorer_continues_after_sql_error.
3. Re-provision both Neon mirrors and regenerate their verification
   fingerprints. This is an external infrastructure action requiring per-action
   authorization.
4. Re-run the affected C1-C3 attempts. This is a demonstrable failure outside
   the evaluated system under the protocol's rerun policy, so it is a
   permitted rerun rather than an answer-dependent one; record the disposition
   before re-running.
5. Audit the other 16 databases for the same class of silent skip even though
   their table counts currently reconcile.
acceptance_criteria: Dump-file resolution rejects capitalization-only mismatches with an explicit error and a regression test covers it. scorer_omitted_tables is empty for mental_healths_large and organ_transplant_large. Both mirrors re-provisioned under per-action authorization, verification.table_count equals 55 and 57, and fingerprints regenerated as new append-only records. Affected C1-C3 attempts re-run under a recorded pre-run disposition. All 18 databases audited for the same class of silent skip.
notes:
2026-08-29 code fix landed for steps 1 and 5; steps 2, 3 and 4 remain and need
human authorization. Working tree only, nothing committed.

WHAT CHANGED

New module src/omni_benchmark/dump_coverage.py resolves a restore order against
a dump directory independently of the database client, so the same resolution
can be audited offline. index_dump_files maps each casefolded dump stem to its
file and raises DumpCoverageError when two files differ only in capitalization.
describe_dump_coverage reports rather than raises, returning load paths in
restore order plus missing tables, case mismatches, and contradicted omissions.

restore_database in database_postgres.py now delegates resolution to that module
and raises on any contradicted omission, naming both the omitted table and the
dump file that contradicts it. Identifier validation still runs over restore
order and omissions before any filesystem or client work, so the path-traversal
and symlink guards are unchanged.

New CLI subcommand: omni_benchmark.database_cli verify-dump-coverage
--dump-root <root> --restore-order <path>. It reports every inventory database
without contacting PostgreSQL and exits 1 if any database is incomplete.

DIVERGENCE FROM THE ORIGINAL ACCEPTANCE CRITERION

This bead was filed asking that resolution reject capitalization-only
mismatches. Implementing that would have left the restore broken, because the
mismatch is in the restore order rather than in the dump: facilities.sql
contains CREATE TABLE public.facilities, and the schema file declares the table
unquoted and lower case. The filename is only a selector; the file carries the
authoritative identifier. Resolution is therefore case-insensitive and
unambiguous, and the strictness moved to where the data loss actually happened:
an omission can no longer be satisfied by a case variant. Case-insensitive
collisions inside one directory are rejected outright.

AUDIT ACROSS ALL 18 DATABASES

Run against the real upstream dumps at
data/raw/livesqlbench-large-v1/extracted/postgre_table_dumps_large with
config/databases/restore-order-large-v1.json. Exit code 1.

  mental_healths_large     55 ordered, 21 resolvable, 34 contradicted omissions
  organ_transplant_large   57 ordered, 20 resolvable, 37 contradicted omissions
  other 16 databases       complete

Totals: 71 contradicted omissions, 0 genuinely missing dump files. The single
omission on labor_certification_applications_large is genuine; that table has no
dump file under any capitalization, so 50 ordered resolve to 49 and the database
reports complete. This confirms the defect is confined to the two databases and
that no other database is silently truncated.

TESTS

tests/test_dump_coverage.py, seven cases covering collision rejection,
case-insensitive resolution, contradicted omissions, genuine upstream
omissions, missing dumps, and order preservation. Three regression cases added
to tests/test_database_postgres.py and two to tests/test_database_cli.py, the
latter driven by the real committed inventory and restore order. Full suite:
1,512 passed, 3 expected environment skips. Ruff check and format clean.

REMAINING

Step 2, clearing scorer_omitted_tables and scorer_continues_after_sql_error for
the two databases, is deliberately not done here. That edit changes
config/databases/livesqlbench-large-v1.json, whose SHA-256 is pinned as
inventory_sha256 in config/conditions/direct-database-targets-v1.json and
verified against published run sidecars by direct_database_loader.py. It also
must land together with step 3, since clearing the omissions without
re-provisioning leaves verification.table_count inconsistent, and re-provisioning
without clearing them drops the same 71 tables again. Steps 3 and 4 are external
actions requiring per-action authorization.

Step 1 (code fix) committed as f5f756b on main: new dump_coverage module,
restore_database resolution rewritten, verify-dump-coverage subcommand.
7 files, 516 insertions, 18 deletions. Suite 1512 passed, branch coverage 84.23%.

Implementation diverges from this bead's original acceptance criterion, which asked
resolution to reject capitalization-only mismatches. That would have left the restore
broken: facilities.sql contains CREATE TABLE public.facilities and the schema declares
the table unquoted, so the file is correct and only the filename differs. Resolution is
case-insensitive; the strictness moved to omissions, which are now refused when any
capitalization of the file exists. Reasoning recorded in D-071.

Steps 2-4 remain, each needing per-action authorization:
 2. clear scorer_omitted_tables and scorer_continues_after_sql_error for
    mental_healths_large and organ_transplant_large in
    config/databases/livesqlbench-large-v1.json, and correct verification.table_count
    (21 to 55, 20 to 57). That file's SHA-256 is pinned as inventory_sha256 in
    config/conditions/direct-database-targets-v1.json and verified against published
    run sidecars, so the pin has to move with it.
 3. re-provision both Neon mirrors from the full dump set.
 4. re-run the affected C1-C3 attempts under the rerun policy (infrastructure failure
    outside the evaluated system, not a wrong answer).
Steps 2 and 3 land together or the recorded table_count contradicts the deployed
database.


RETRACTED 2026-08-29. This bead's premise is false and its fix is reverted.

The pinned upstream loader init-databases_postgresql_large_v1.sh lines 118-127
resolves each dump as <table>.sql with an exact filename match and skips with a
warning on a miss. Its list spells the table Facilities; the archive ships only
facilities.sql; the pinned image is Linux. So the OFFICIAL reference database is
built without those 34 and 37 tables. This repository reproduced that on purpose,
which docs/database-setup.md already stated.

Arithmetic: mental_healths_large_template holds 57 dump files, 21 with capital
letters, and verification.table_count is 21. 55 declared minus 21 loaded is 34,
element for element the committed scorer_omitted_tables. organ_transplant_large
gives 20 of 57 with 37 omitted. The restore was never truncated relative to its
target.

Commit f5f756b would have loaded the lowercase files, building two databases
holding tables the scorer's does not, and breaking comparability with published
LiveSQLBench numbers. It also made the correct configuration unrestorable, since
it refused a declared omission whose case variant exists. Its behavior is reverted.

Kept in corrected form: dump_coverage and verify-dump-coverage, reframed from
completeness to fidelity. They now assert scorer_omitted_tables equals the set the
official loader actually skips. Against the real archive all 18 databases pass,
exit 0.

The real finding moves to the follow-up bead: 27 dev-A questions are unanswerable
in the official environment and need an exclusion record, not a repair.
Full reasoning in docs/research-log.md D-072; D-071 is marked retracted.
close_reason: Refuted: upstream loader behavior, faithfully reproduced. Fix reverted. See D-072.

title: Reconcile dev-A coverage rule with C4 deployment footprint before v5 dispatch
description:
The dev-A intervention preregistration committed at 82f0d4f cannot be satisfied
by the C4 arm that is currently prepared for launch. This is a frame decision on
a human-controlled surface (scoring definitions), not an agent task, and it must
be settled BEFORE the v5 dispatch, because settling it after any C4 number
exists converts it into a post-hoc frame change.

ARITHMETIC

experiments/planned-dev-a-interventions-v1.json states:
- common_evaluation.promotion_condition: C4 is the promotion condition for
  E01-E03.
- common_evaluation.full_dev_a_requirement: an intervention that cannot be
  evaluated on all 154 dev-A questions is INCONCLUSIVE and cannot be promoted.
- stopping_rule: stop early if full dev-A coverage cannot be achieved.

The prepared C4 baseline v5 resolves ten deployment targets, and its dev-A
scoring gate in docs/human-decisions.md is
--expected-official-scoreable-questions 85.

154 dev-A questions span 18 databases. C4 is deployed on 10. At most 85 of 154
dev-A questions are C4-scoreable. Therefore every intervention E01-E03 is
INCONCLUSIVE by construction and the stopping rule fires before E01 begins.

Direct-side coverage is separately incomplete. Of 154 dev-A questions, 32 are
unreachable today:
- mental_healths_large (9) and organ_transplant_large (9): benchmark gold SQL
  does not execute against the restored databases; see omni-benchmark-2j9.
- archeology_scan_large (5) and cybermarket_pattern_large (9): excluded by
  pre-run disposition in config/conditions/public-baseline-exclusions-v1.json,
  scope public-only-c1-c3-baseline.

Counts derived by joining data/manifests/dev_a_ids.txt against the public
selected_database field of data/manifests/eligible_questions.jsonl. No gold,
hidden annotation, or test-split content was read.

OPTIONS

A. Amend full_dev_a_requirement to the C4-deployed frame: all dev-A questions in
   the ten deployed databases, with the frame fixed and committed before the
   first intervention. Cheap, committable today, preserves preregistration
   integrity as long as it lands before any C4 result exists.

B. Hold the 154 rule and wait for omni-benchmark-dih.17 to deploy all 18
   databases. Stronger evaluation, but gated on dih.17.2 and dih.17.3, which are
   open compiler defects.

Independent of A or B: cybermarket_pattern_large can be recovered now. Its
external reader credential is already repaired and verified per the exclusion
record; the exclusion persists only because the original launch evidence
predates the fix. Re-running it into the direct baseline recovers 9 dev-A
questions.

NOTE ON THE SEALED RUN

The development-frame choice does not relieve dih.17. D-046 records the plan as
running C4 once all 18 isolated deployments pass validation and exact readback,
and the split was stratified by database, so the sealed test requires C4 on
every database regardless of what is decided here. Option A buys a development
signal earlier; it does not shorten the path to Freeze B.
acceptance_criteria: A committed decision selecting option A or option B, landed before any public-c4-baseline-v5 result exists. If A, experiments/planned-dev-a-interventions-v1.json records the deployed-frame coverage rule and the fixed database list. If B, omni-benchmark-aez.7.1 stays blocked until omni-benchmark-dih.17 reports 18 validated deployments. Either way the disposition of mental_healths_large, organ_transplant_large, archeology_scan_large, and cybermarket_pattern_large is recorded with the same evidence discipline as the existing exclusion config.
notes:
2026-08-29 correction to the option set. Option B as written is not reachable.
omni-benchmark-2j9 is CLOSED as refuted: both databases match committed
schema/content fingerprints and all 81 receipts bind the correct attested
read-only target. Separately, all 54 unscorable dev-A attempts carry
failure_category gold_statement_error, exactly mental_healths_large 27 plus
organ_transplant_large 27. So the benchmark gold does not execute there while
the restore is provably correct, and no amount of deployment work in
omni-benchmark-dih.17 recovers those 18 dev-A questions. Full 154-question
dev-A coverage is therefore unachievable by anyone, and the preregistered
full_dev_a_requirement must be reframed rather than waited out. The remaining
decision is only what the frame is.

Two hypotheses for the two databases were tested and refuted today. Missing
preprocess step: no question in any of the 18 databases has non-empty
preprocess_sql. Schema qualification or search_path: the committed schema files
for both databases create unqualified public-schema tables, and neither
postgres_execution.py nor direct_sql_capture.py sets search_path.

Leading untested hypothesis: the per-database read-only reader credential holds
catalog access but lacks SELECT on data tables. That fits every observation at
once, including the ones that refuted the earlier readings: catalog
introspection succeeds, every data-table reference fails regardless of
condition, benchmark gold fails, and a catalog-based schema fingerprint still
matches exactly because permissions are not part of it. Direct precedent exists
in this project: cybermarket_pattern_large was excluded after its database
privilege preflight failed, and its external reader credential was later
repaired and verified. Test is one read-only SELECT against one data table per
database using the attested reader. That is a diagnostic, not a rerun, and it
does not require any credential mutation. If it confirms, the disposition is a
grant repair and 18 dev-A questions plus their share of the sealed test are
recovered; if it refutes, the disposition is an exclusion record with the same
evidence discipline as public-baseline-exclusions-v1.json.

Note that SQLSTATE is currently discarded at direct_sql_capture.py, which is
why this could not be settled from existing telemetry. See omni-benchmark-bfb.
2026-08-29 second correction to the option set; supersedes the note above. The
18 dev-A questions on mental_healths_large and organ_transplant_large are
recoverable. omni-benchmark-39b establishes that restore dropped 34 and 37
tables through case-sensitive dump-file resolution, the data ships in the
upstream dump as lowercase files, and the benchmark gold is not defective. The
reader-grant hypothesis recorded in the previous note is refuted; no live query
was needed to settle it. Once 39b is repaired, dev-A coverage returns to 145 of
154, short only by archeology_scan_large (5) unless its exclusion is revisited,
and by cybermarket_pattern_large (9) unless it is re-run. Decide wk0 after 39b
lands rather than against the current numbers.

title: Authorize finite-Decimal repair in frozen scorers
description: The option-A dev-A scoring run published nothing and stopped on decimal.InvalidOperation while normalizing an official candidate result. No question identity, value, or correctness was inspected; output root stayed absent and score clones returned to zero. The documented frozen contract says Decimal/float values are rounded half-up, but Python Decimal.quantize uses the ambient 28-digit context and fails on otherwise finite values with more digits. A general implementation repair can use a local context sized from the finite operand for both frozen scorers, with no question-specific logic and no change to the documented rounding rule. Because this changes scorer behavior after dev-A release, human authorization is required. Choice A (recommended): authorize the contract-conformance repair, keep scorer semantic identities because the documented policy is unchanged, add regression tests, rerun all gates, then permit one clean scoring restart. Choice B: retain the exact frozen implementation behavior, classify this as scorer_policy_error, and block dev-A scoring/MVP pending a separately approved treatment. Do not restart or publish until response.

title: Two database environments fail uniformly across all conditions; classification and restore both in question
description:
Found 2026-08-28 23:05Z while monitoring public-baseline-v1-direct-16db-continuation-1
at 307 captures. Not acted on: the classification question is a human-controlled surface.

OBSERVATION

  organ_transplant_large    0 ok / 39 attempts   (c1 0/13, c2 0/13, c3 0/13)
  mental_healths_large      4 ok / 42 attempts   (c1 2/14, c2 1/14, c3 1/14)

Those two databases account for all 48 database_statement_error in the run. The other
eight databases seen so far have zero. The failure is total, flat across three different
scaffolds, and confined to two databases. That pattern is what a broken environment looks
like; it is not what a model-capability difference looks like, because a capability
difference would vary by condition and these do not.

Supporting detail from organ_transplant_large/c1/organ_transplant_3-r1: the attempt
degrades from a three-table join, to a simpler join, to SELECT * FROM transplant_matching
LIMIT 5, which is the shape of a client probing after repeated rejections.

NOT ESTABLISHED

No error text was recovered. attempt.trace.jsonl records metadata_sha256 rather than
message bodies, which is the telemetry contract working as designed, and the benchmark
databases are not in the local postgres instance, so no direct query was attempted. A
broken restore and a genuinely hostile schema are still both consistent with the evidence.
Someone with the database environment in hand can settle it in one query.

IMPACT ON EVERY CONDITION-LEVEL NUMBER REPORTED TODAY

                     all 10 DBs      excluding the two
  c1                  52.9%              68.8%
  c2                  71.3%              95.9%
  c3                  50.5%              67.1%
  c2 vs c3        z=3.04 p=0.0023    z=4.53 p<0.0001
  c1 vs c3             --             z=0.23 p=0.8190

D-066 survives and sharpens rather than dissolving: C2 answers 96% on the clean eight
while C1 and C3 are indistinguishable at about 68%. But every absolute rate in D-066 and
in the RUN-CLASSES census is depressed roughly 16 points by these two databases.

THE CLASSIFICATION QUESTION, FOR A HUMAN

These 81 attempts carry failure_origin=evaluated_system. If the environments are broken
the origin is infrastructure, and the protocol rerun policy covers exactly that case
("reruns require a demonstrable failure outside the evaluated system"). Scoring them as
the system failing 81 questions would understate every condition. Reclassification is a
custody and scoring surface; proposing, not changing.

ALSO WORTH CHECKING

The run id says 16db and ten distinct databases have appeared at 307 of 518 captures.
Either more are pending in the remaining attempts or the deployment covers fewer
databases than the name implies. Not investigated.
notes:
2026-08-28 public-only definitive diagnostic (no labels, answers, or correctness read): recomputed the existing database_fingerprint through the external private PG environments with default_transaction_read_only=on. mental_healths_large exactly matches committed PostgreSQL 180006, 21 tables, 33582 rows, schema SHA-256 d0758ce810a8bcc949121f55542e82e5a9fe2816bdd064a475f7d47643505a01, content SHA-256 4887ac64a13b2f164d50e55f64bf1e732e04adf9319e646680c98b836a0d3d89. organ_transplant_large exactly matches 180006, 20 tables, 8970 rows, schema SHA-256 061cffb1893b6c4e770e93a27b86f96c3221037fded630af0cff5bde914f7111, content SHA-256 39d5fb50801f758c6aa085995d4110ed3bc85b03f709aec62fd33e03612fd176. All 42 mental-health and 39 organ-transplant capture receipts have zero committed runtime database-binding mismatches, with balanced C1-C3 coverage; fresh attestation confirms the role is read-only and has no execute privilege on non-system functions. The restore/target hypothesis is refuted. No demonstrable failure outside the evaluated system exists, so the protocol does not authorize reruns. No failure-origin or scoring definition was changed.
DIAGNOSIS CONFIRMED FROM ARTIFACTS - partial/absent restore, not a capability difference

Method: join attempt.action-evidence.json (retains exploratory_sql, keyed by
trace_seq) to attempt.trace.jsonl (retains per-seq status and
database_query_delta). Classify each executed query by whether it touches only
catalog relations (information_schema, pg_class, pg_namespace, pg_attribute) or
real data tables.

Successful executions on data tables, per database:

  residential_data 73, virtual_idol 60, planets_data 51, labor_certification 44,
  reverse_logistics 39, solar_panel 36, sports_events 34, fake_account 32,
  robot_fault 21, museum_artifact 14, polar_equipment 6, cross_border 2,
  mental_healths 0, organ_transplant 0

organ_transplant_large: 45 successful executions, ALL catalog-only, 0 on any data
table across 39 attempts and 3 conditions. Every user table is 0-for-N
(transplant_matching 0/46, clinical 0/27, compatibility_metrics 0/24,
recipients_immunology 0/22, risk_evaluation 0/16, ...).
mental_healths_large: 23 successful executions, ALL catalog-only, 0 on data
tables across 42 attempts (assessmentbasics 0/47, encounters 0/42,
treatmentbasics 0/36, facilities 0/28, ...).

The connection is up and the catalog answers, so this is not unreachability. No
data table is queryable in either environment. Consistent with an absent restore,
or with tables living in a schema the connection's search_path does not include.
The models kept guessing table names from the documented schema file, which is
what happens when their information_schema probes return zero rows.

I previously wrote "broken environment, could not confirm" in the briefing. The
strong claim was under-evidenced at the time and the shape is now established
from the artifacts. It remains for whoever holds the DB credentials to run the
one confirming query; I have no .env in either worktree:

  \dt  -- or:
  SELECT table_schema, count(*) FROM information_schema.tables
  WHERE table_schema NOT IN ('pg_catalog','information_schema')
  GROUP BY 1;

If that returns zero rows for these two databases the restore is the fault.
DECISIVE: the model used only PUBLISHED table names and every one was rejected.

Follow-up to the catalog-only finding. Compared the table names appearing in
executed queries against the benchmark's own published schema
(data/raw/livesqlbench-large-v1/schema/<db>/<db>_schema.txt, the same file that
feeds C1's provided context).

                          documented   refs in FAILED   refs in OK
                             tables       queries        queries
  organ_transplant_large        37       168 (11 tbls)    0 (0)
  mental_healths_large          34       230 ( 9 tbls)    0 (0)
  planets_data_large  [control] 29         0 ( 0)       122 (7)

organ_transplant_large: administrative_and_review, clinical,
compatibility_metrics, demographics, function_and_recovery, hla_info, hospitals,
recipients_demographics, recipients_immunology, risk_evaluation,
transplant_matching - every one referenced from the published schema, every one
rejected, none ever succeeding.

mental_healths_large: assessmentbasics, assessmentsocialanddiagnosis,
assessmentsymptomsandrisk, encounters, facilities, patientclinicaltrials,
patients, treatmentbasics, treatmentoutcomes - same pattern.

The control shows the healthy shape: documented names appear in successful
queries and never in failed ones.

This eliminates the model-defect explanation. The system was not inventing
tables; it used the names the benchmark publishes, and the database rejected all
of them while answering catalog queries normally. The environment does not match
its own published schema.

No database access was needed for this. Confirmation via information_schema is
still worth having but is no longer load-bearing.
INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED BY THE SCORER: gold_statement_error on all 54 attempts.

public-direct-baseline-dev-a-scores-v1 scored the dev-A partition with both
frozen scorers. 54 of 420 attempts came back status=unscorable with
failure_category=gold_statement_error, and they are exactly:

  mental_healths      27
  organ_transplant    27

Nothing else. gold_statement_error means the benchmark's own reference SQL failed
to execute against those databases. The gold query cannot run there either.

This is independent of my action-evidence reconstruction and reaches the same
place by a different route. The evaluated system was never the variable: the
reference answer fails on the same two environments where every published table
name was rejected. Diagnosis is closed. What remains is the repair and the
custody question, not the cause.

Consequence, and it is good news for the numbers: the scorer already excluded
these 18 questions per condition, so the dev-A accuracy figures are computed on
122 clean questions per condition and are NOT contaminated. The correction I
recommended (report the 437-capture figures as primary) is already applied
upstream of scoring by construction.
close_reason: Refuted by exact live parity: both databases match committed schema/content fingerprints and all 81 receipts bind the correct attested read-only target. No external infrastructure failure was demonstrated, so no rerun or classification change is authorized.

title: Freeze reconciled direct baseline by content hash
description: The authorized 630-trial public direct baseline is split across 112 preserved source attempts and a 518-attempt infrastructure continuation. Existing reconciliation proves counts but does not emit one immutable content-addressed selection manifest. Add the smallest deterministic freeze artifact that binds every selected generation/run pair, exact source and continuation identities, committed exclusions, and complete coverage before any train-label release. Do not inspect answers or correctness and do not mutate either live worktree.
design: Hypothesis: extending the existing result-independent continuation reconciliation with a deterministic selection manifest is sufficient to freeze the public direct baseline without changing the protocol or copying run artifacts. The manifest records identity, disposition, and hashes only; it never parses answers beyond existing generation/run validators. Implement tests first in a new isolated worktree based on the live control commit, then run focused and full gates. No commit or push without explicit authorization.
acceptance_criteria: TDD proves incomplete reconciliation cannot freeze; complete reconciliation yields exactly 630 unique trials with 112 preserved and 518 continuation selections; every selected generation and run manifest is revalidated and SHA-bound; output is canonical, mode 0600, O_EXCL, and contains no correctness or forbidden fields; CLI uses only the authorized source/continuation identities and no live provider or credential access.

Added deterministic complete-only 112-preserved + 518-continuation content-addressed selection manifest, per-entry generation/run revalidation and SHA binding, canonical confined mode-0600 O_EXCL writer, and authorized exact-path freeze CLI with no provider/credential path. Gates: 17 focused passed; 51 affected passed; full 1424 passed, 5 skipped, 84.45% branch coverage; Ruff and format clean. Implementation remains uncommitted; do not freeze or preserve the continuation tree until the sole service exits.

Result-independent reconciliation: complete=true, 518 continuation, 112 preserved, 630/630 total, zero missing; manifest 751a2a7081958d3d35d051ca47d9f62481d3df082048c7644b125bc093179717. After exit, copied the ignored tree to main; source/copy both 2959 files, 22308271 bytes, normalized inventory SHA-256 633283e18867b48be8e476f7bbdfd048e4ce8e4f4a846ebb32f65cceeb3ae57f. title: Fix continuation child runtime package binding
description: The committed continuation launcher runs each child from the exact execution workspace, but Python imports omni_benchmark from the parent continuation worktree. acceptance_criteria: A focused test reproduces the wrong-parent package import before the fix and passes afterward; child process imports omni_benchmark from execution_workspace; parent launcher remains executable from continuation workspace; exact system commit and manifest validation are unchanged; focused and full tests plus Ruff pass; independent reviewer approves.
notes:
Completed in local commit 5748eba228bc8cca824ec94472a1b09da9b4c856. RED reproduced subprocess package miss; GREEN binds child PYTHONPATH to execution_workspace/src. Focused 21 passed; full 1417 passed/5 environment skips; branch coverage 84.46%; Ruff and diff checks pass. Independent code-reviewer APPROVED with zero findings. Parent continuation remains importable from continuation worktree, child direct_prepared_attempt resolves from /tmp/omni-benchmark-direct-continuation-live-5be/src. System commit constant and manifest unchanged; manifest SHA-256 remains 751a2a7081958d3d35d051ca47d9f62481d3df082048c7644b125bc093179717. No live run, credentials, gold, hidden, test, or dev-B access.
Verified the fix against the live continuation run rather than by reading the diff. All three baseline_direct_attempt.py children of public-baseline-v1-direct-16db-continuation-1 carry PYTHONPATH=/tmp/omni-benchmark-direct-continuation-live-5be/src in /proc/<pid>/environ. Parent runs from /tmp/omni-benchmark-direct-continuation at 5748eba; children import from the execution worktree at 5be315e, matching the git_commit recorded in each run.json. Reproduced under the children's exact environment: omni_benchmark resolves to -live-5be/src and direct_public_search.MAX_SCHEMA_MATCHES is 4 (the 5be315e value), not the 8 in 5748eba. PYTHONPATH precedes the editable install because __editable__.omni_benchmark-0.1.0.pth is a plain path entry, not a MetaPathFinder. The binding is load-bearing: the two trees diverge on the direct path, so anything clearing PYTHONPATH would swap the C1 schema-retrieval budget while run.json continued to claim 5be315e. Worth an explicit assertion in the child rather than relying on env inheritance.

title: Enforce human authorization for production run launches in the control plane
description:
On 2026-08-28 the main benchmark agent launched the paid production run public-c4-baseline-v1-20260828 at 19:03:12Z, roughly ten seconds after canary v6's final attempt finalized at 19:03:01Z, with no human authorization. Canary success is a precondition for the 129-task run, not an authorization to launch it, but that distinction existed only as a recorded note in agent memory and the frontier record. A recorded precondition did not stop a run that bills omni-production-baseline-v1.

The run then produced 6 answered attempts followed by 5 consecutive adapter_transport_error failures (19:04:25-19:04:55Z, all five databases), every one of them misattributed as failure_origin=evaluated_system while also carrying harness_failure=adapter_transport_error. So the unauthorized launch also generated contaminated C4 records against the primary deliverable, with cost_usd null and cost_source unavailable throughout.

This blocks the results report because the report's headline C4 number depends on production runs whose launch conditions are actually enforced. An unenforced gate will fire again at the next launch point.
acceptance_criteria: Production and sealed-scope run launches require an explicit, recorded human authorization token or equivalent control-plane check that the agent cannot self-issue; canary success alone cannot satisfy it. Attempting a gated launch without authorization fails closed with a clear error and writes no attempt records. The check is fault-tested, not merely declared: a test demonstrates an unauthorized launch attempt is refused. Distinguish precondition (canary clean) from authorization (human approval) in both the control plane and the protocol docs. Does not weaken existing custody, metering, or rerun gates.

title: Bound direct schema context to prevent model-budget exhaustion
description: The immutable public-baseline-v1-full archeology_scan_1:C1 attempt exhausted the per-turn Claude budget after 5 schema inspections and 5 SQL executions, consuming 1,114,427 tokens and USD 7.4942295 without an answer. The current schema search permits up to four whole tables / 64 KiB per call, and the accumulated conversation repeatedly re-bills those payloads. Implement the smallest general public-only retrieval/context bound that prevents this failure without question-specific routing or hidden/gold inputs; preserve competent schema discovery and C1-C3 fairness.
design: Trace-first, local change before architecture: inspect the five public schema results and reduce redundant/irrelevant context using a general deterministic bound or deduplication. Do not raise budgets, special-case archeology/question text, or weaken capture/custody. Preserve old failed attempt immutably.
acceptance_criteria: RED test reproduces bounded-search/context accumulation causing model-budget failure or payload excess; fix applies uniformly across databases/conditions, has deterministic limits and provenance, and does not use question IDs/hidden labels. archeology_scan_1:C1 public replay answers within the frozen attempt budget or the database is explicitly excluded with evidence. Focused/full direct tests and Ruff pass; independent code review clears; cost/token delta is recorded before full fan-out.
notes:
2026-08-28T17:40Z TDD: RED showed four matching whole tables permit repeated schema context growth. Minimal cross-database structural intervention caps schema retrieval at two whole-table matches while retaining the existing 64 KiB per-call guard. Replaying the five public archeology failure-trace retrieval queries mechanically reduced cumulative schema payload from 187,261 to 91,439 bytes (-51.2%) and stable-ID occurrences from 468 to 227. No question/database rules or hidden inputs. 506 focused direct tests and full 1,385-test suite pass; Ruff clean; independent review approved. Live replay2 at commit 3395421 ended refused/agent_refusal with no SQL/result: 732,563 tokens (-34.3%), USD 4.3204315 (-42.4%), 125.783s, 10 tools (6 schema/4 SQL), 4 DB queries, versus prior model_budget_error at 1,114,427 tokens/USD 7.4942295/131.972s/10 tools/5 queries. The intervention removes budget exhaustion but does not make this item answer; outcome remains FOLLOW UP / product tradeoff rather than a correctness KEEP.
First live incidence on the 16db continuation. cross_border_6 C1 captured failure_class=model_budget_error, failure_origin=evaluated_system, generation_outcome=errored, database_query_count=0, cost $3.82 (the most expensive attempt in the segment), latency 60.8s. Zero database queries with an exhausted budget on the schema-retrieval condition is the signature this bug describes: context spent on schema before a single query is issued.

Rate at 20:10Z is 1 of 11 captures (9%). If it holds across the 518-attempt continuation that is ~47 attempts concentrated in C1 and roughly $180 of the $2000 ceiling.

Classification is the load-bearing part and is a human-controlled surface, so flagging rather than changing. Attributing these to evaluated_system scores them as the system failing the question. If the cause is a harness-side unbounded schema context, the origin is arguably the harness, and under the rerun policy ('reruns require a demonstrable failure outside the evaluated system') reclassification would make these attempts rerunnable. The opposite reading is also defensible: the system was given a schema and managed its budget badly. This needs a human decision before scoring, not after seeing results.

title: Wrong-answer is the dominant failure class (245 of 366 scored) and has no owner
description:
From public-direct-baseline-dev-a-scores-v1, dev-A, official Soft EX:

  wrong_answer       245
  refused_or_error    67
  correct             54

The direct comparators mostly produce runnable SQL that returns the wrong result.
Per condition, wrong answers are C1 80, C2 91, C3 74 out of 122 scoreable.

The two open failure beads together cover 67 of 366 scored attempts:
omni-benchmark-dx3 (refusal, 80 captures) and dih.5.4.2.4.4.2.2.2 (model budget,
17 captures). The largest class by a factor of three has no bead.

Scope: characterize why runnable SQL returns wrong results. Candidate axes, to be
tested rather than assumed - join grain and fan-out, aggregation level, null and
filter semantics, ambiguous entity resolution, and the representability gap
already recorded for business definitions that cannot be compiled into executable
semantic objects without cardinality/grain/identity information.

Do this on dev-A only. Any intervention must be classified for generality before
it is made; question-specific changes are prohibited.

Note the accuracy ceiling this implies: at C2 23.8% [16.2, 31.3] the headroom is
almost entirely in this class, so it is where any real gain has to come from.

title: Refusal (no_answer_insufficient_context) is the dominant never-queried mode; needs its own bead
description:
Split out of omni-benchmark-dih.5.4.2.4.4.2.2.2, which is titled for unbounded
direct schema context causing model-budget exhaustion.

At full n on public-baseline-v1-direct-16db-continuation-1 (518 captures):

  no_answer_insufficient_context   80   c1:37 c2:3  c3:40
  model_budget_error               17   c1:7  c2:3  c3:7

63 attempts issued zero database queries: 51 refusals, 12 budget exhaustions.
Refusal is roughly five times more common than the class the P0 bead is named
for, and the near-absence in C2 (3 of 80) says it tracks what reference material
the condition exposes, not the token budget.

These are different mechanisms with different fixes. Bounding schema context
addresses budget exhaustion; it does not address a model that reads the available
context and concludes it cannot answer. Keeping both on one bead was hiding the
larger of the two.

Scope here: characterize why C1 and C3 refuse where C2 does not, and whether the
refusal is correct behavior (the reference genuinely lacks what is needed) or
premature. Note that under Soft EX a refusal and a wrong answer both score zero,
so refusal is not rewarded by the frozen scorers even where it is the better
engineering behavior.

Blocked on omni-benchmark-2j9: 19 of the 80 refusals are on the two databases
with no queryable data tables, where refusal is the correct response to an empty
environment and must not be counted as a system property.

title: Retain SQLSTATE in direct-capture telemetry so failure origin is derivable
description:
postgres_execution._execution_error computes the SQLSTATE and uses it to pick a
kind (timeout / infrastructure / statement), then direct_sql_capture.py:472 keeps
only error.kind:

    except PostgreSQLExecutionError as error:
        self._record_database_queries(max(1, error.statement_index + 1))
        execution = database_failure(f"database_{error.kind}_error")

The SQLSTATE is discarded and appears in no artifact. Consequence: every non-08
SQLSTATE collapses into database_statement_error, so the artifacts cannot
separate 42P01 undefined_table from 42703 undefined_column from a genuine model
SQL defect. That is the difference between a broken benchmark environment and an
incorrect system outcome, and failure_origin is computed from failure_class
alone (direct_capture_telemetry.failure_origin).

This is why the organ_transplant_large / mental_healths_large classification
(omni-benchmark-2j9) had to be reconstructed by joining action-evidence SQL text
to per-seq trace status. That reconstruction works but it is not the contract
doing its job.

Fix: carry sqlstate and statement_index onto the trace event and the capture
receipt for database failures. Purely additive telemetry; does not change any
failure_class value or any origin assignment, so it does not touch a
human-controlled scoring surface.

Do this before Freeze B, since Freeze B commits the failure-classification policy
and the protocol forbids reclassifying after scoring.

title: Automate immutable Claude OAuth lease preflight
description: The direct benchmark needs automated, immutable Claude OAuth lease preparation without live credential refresh. Measurements show a 0700 isolated profile containing a valid access token and minimal non-secret configuration survives pinning and a completed read-only invocation byte-for-byte; cloning is not itself the failure when token headroom exceeds the run and every source identity is quiescent. Build a preflight that selects dedicated identities, verifies no attached sessions, requires access-token headroom greater than maximum run duration plus margin, constructs a 0700 minimal lease, verifies the pinned binary version/SHA, and forbids every writer/refresh process until release.
design: For benchmark runs, refresh-before-freeze and then hold still. Never refresh or copy back underneath verify_unchanged. The general fleet may keep a broker/keepalive, but it must surrender an identity for the entire benchmark lease. Preflight checks: source session count zero; source/lease 0700; credentials 0600; exact minimal config; access-token expiry beyond the scheduled wall bound and margin; refresh token never exercised during lease; exact committed Claude binary version/SHA. Lease artifacts expose only opaque hashes/expiry, never token content. Existing interrupted baseline remains frozen at its committed system configuration.
acceptance_criteria: Synthetic/live-public tests prove 0700 lease creation, minimal config, access-token headroom refusal, attached-session refusal, committed binary version/SHA match, three sequential immutable invocations without source/lease mutation, and fail-closed behavior on any mutation. No mid-run refresh, token copy-back, or competing session. Account-specific lease creation remains outside git and secrets never enter output. Integration is used only when compatible with the frozen baseline or in a separately frozen run.
notes:
Measured launch issue after lease handoff: exact frozen source at 5be315e was rejected because the parent process wrote pycs that child processes recompiled under different Python hash seeds; modules containing unordered constants produced different byte sequences. This is a pre-invocation infrastructure failure. For immediate immutable canary, remove ignored pycs and launch parent+children with PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1. Durable preflight should avoid treating byte-for-byte pyc equality as a source-integrity oracle.
2026-08-28T19:30Z: exact 2.1.250 frozen-transport canary public-baseline-v1-lease-canary-v2-20260828-1525 completed 12/12 at concurrency 3: 11 answered, 1 no_answer_insufficient_context, zero infrastructure failures/retries, 2,161,895 tokens, 5.5811165 measured notional cost. The immediate pyc workaround was PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 from parent launch after moving ignored pycs out of the worktree. Durable preflight change remains separate.
Partial delivery (uncommitted, main worktree). src/omni_benchmark/claude_lease_preflight.py + tests/test_claude_lease_preflight.py (19 tests) implement three of the design's checks: at least one slot; every slot's access-token headroom strictly greater than the attempt bound; and an optional --identity-stable-until wall that refuses to launch when a scheduled rotation lands inside the attempt window. Wired into baseline_batch_cli._execute_live immediately before run_baseline_batch. Error messages carry a sha256 slot identity, never a path or token.

Still unimplemented from the design: source session count zero, source/lease 0700 and credentials 0600 assertions, exact-minimal-config assertion, pinned binary version/SHA check. Slot-to-source correspondence is deliberately excluded from the harness module (a deployment fact, not a property of the evaluated system) and belongs to the lease-building operator tooling.

Measured correction to the design's premise: claude-refresh-all iterates /home/ds/.claude-homes/account{1..5} only and has no reference to /home/ds/.claude-leases, so a cron pass cannot mutate a lease directory or trip verify_unchanged(). The binding constraint on a run is the lease access-token expiry (currently 2026-08-29T02:54Z), not the 6h cron boundary. Whether a source-home refresh invalidates the lease's access token is still unobserved; the 23:00Z pass is the first test.
Coverage gap found and closed. The preflight was wired only into baseline_batch_cli._execute_live, but baseline_continuation_cli._execute constructs LiveBaselineDispatcher and calls run_baseline_batch directly without passing through it. The live 518-attempt continuation dispatches through the continuation path, so the gate would not have fired on the launch that will actually hit its credential wall. Now gated at the top of _execute, before the dispatcher and the database environment directory are constructed, so a refusal costs nothing; --identity-stable-until added to the continuation parser for parity. Test test_execute_refuses_when_a_lease_expires_inside_the_attempt_bound asserts run_baseline_batch is never reached. Suite 1443 passed / 3 skipped, ruff clean. Uncommitted in main.

General lesson worth carrying: this codebase has two live-dispatch entrypoints, and a preflight is only as good as the narrowest one it covers. Any future launch gate needs wiring into both.
Comparator OAuth pool is now four slots. Leased /home/ds/.claude-leases/omni-a5 from account5 (fingerprint 7eb167203f8d, matches source); .lease-rebuild.sh and the lane monitor cover slots 1, 3, 4, 5. account2 is permanently retired: never leased, never counted as capacity, and its logged-out state is expected. Its removal from /home/ds/.gc/account-identity.map is a fleet action outside this repo; until then claude-refresh-all alerts on it every 6h.

Dispatch timeout default lowered 1800s -> 900s in both live entrypoints. Slowest attempt observed on the 16db continuation was 156s, so 900s keeps a wide margin for slower databases while capping what one wedged attempt holds a slot for, and it halves the token headroom verify_lease_window demands since the attempt bound is what it compares tokens against. Future launches only. Test: test_dispatch_timeout_default_bounds_a_stuck_attempt_without_failing_slow_ones. Suite 1444 passed / 3 skipped, ruff clean, all still uncommitted in main.
2026-08-29 main-only consolidation: the tracked uncommitted lease-preflight integration was deliberately excluded from canonical main because credential/OAuth/lease work is out of scope. Its complete tracked patch is preserved in stash main-pre-consolidation-tracked-20260829T1748-0400 (full stash patch SHA-256 1320b69b9335b330c14e245bccfdee1da761453b54da62c03d81ea87b578ef80); untracked src/omni_benchmark/claude_lease_preflight.py and tests/test_claude_lease_preflight.py remain untouched in the main worktree. Resume only in an isolated worktree under operator-owned lease authority; do not apply the whole stash to main.

title: Specify LiveSQLBench Large-v1 evaluation and pre-gold protocol
description: Design a rigorous, publishable Omni evaluation of non-CRUD LiveSQLBench Large-v1. Research only public materials, resolve experimental decisions collaboratively, create a deterministic leakage-resistant train/test protocol, and establish the durable project goal before any gold-answer access.
design: Primary estimand: Given an existing semantic model for a database, how accurately does Omni answer previously unseen analytical questions, and do semantic-layer/harness improvements developed on other questions generalize to those unseen questions? Use deterministic 231 train / 101 test question-level split across all 18 DBs, with database as primary stratification and public metadata balanced where feasible. Full public schema and HKB for every DB are available during model construction; held-out question ground truth and hidden annotations are inaccessible until freeze. Database-specific model changes based only on that DB's training questions are allowed. Secondary: 18-fold leave-one-database-out transformation portability within the 231-question development partition. Tertiary: preregistered raw-schema / HKB-context / Omni-semantic ablation if fair and technically feasible.
acceptance_criteria: Public benchmark structure and knowledge-base semantics are documented; eligible non-CRUD manifest and deterministic representative split design are specified; gold-access guard is enforced; user and agent reach shared understanding on material experimental forks; resulting goal is recorded.
notes:
Custody decision: hard human-custody seal. Before private data: commit eligible manifest, deterministic 231/101 split and IDs, extraction/evaluation boundary, and EVALUATION_PROTOCOL.md; precommit only format-independent tooling if attachment schema is not sufficiently documented. User keeps untouched attachment outside agent-accessible workspace and records SHA-256 without content inspection. A deterministic train-only extraction releases 231 private records to ignored private/train; hidden test fields never enter development. Freeze all semantic models/harness/config/prompts/versions and commit a machine-readable freeze manifest. A dedicated sealed evaluator receives the untouched source, selects only precommitted 101 IDs, executes comparison, and emits scores/permitted aggregates without gold SQL. Record source SHA-256, split commit, final commit, run timestamp/config, artifacts. Public text/metadata for all 332 may stay committed. Hidden external_knowledge/test cases for train may be available but their permitted experimental role is still to be resolved.
Public reconnaissance (official releases only; no gold accessed): HF commit a418e108d5cbb4cf9b783a928eff5e924ad2460d; official harness commit e15cd221267e06fabfaf6a3d4a69308280ce9a7c. Public JSONL has 480 rows: 332 Query and 148 Management. Query tasks span all 18 DBs (10-24 each), 181 high_level=true / 151 false; no public difficulty_tier; private sol_sql/external_knowledge/test_cases arrays empty. Across HKBs: 1,090 definitions (430 calculation, 462 domain, 198 value illustration), 560 dependent definitions and 945 declared edges. Official SELECT evaluator removes DISTINCT from both SQLs, executes with 60s timeout, normalizes dates/JSON/numerics (default 2 decimals), then compares ordered lists when conditions.order=true and sets otherwise. gas-city reuse: provenance ledger, pinned build, isolated fixtures, mutation-proven assertions, browser-authored Omni models/topics and three-leg outside-SQL/Omni-SQL/Omni-topic parity.
Held-out matrix decision: freeze and score all four conditions together on the 101 test questions. C1 Raw SQL = schema/raw representation/no enforcement. C2 HKB-reference SQL = schema+HKB/raw HKB available via reasonable programmatic/search access/optional use. C3 Omni-model SQL = schema+HKB/exported Omni semantic model available via equivalent reference access/optional use. C4 Governed Omni = schema+HKB/Omni semantic model/enforced semantic compilation and production validation. Primary endpoint is frozen C4 execution accuracy. Prespecified confirmatory paired contrasts: C2-C1 business knowledge; C3-C2 structured semantic representation; C4-C3 enforcement/governance/harness; C4-C1 total system effect. Freeze and reasonably develop all four on train. Match exogenous resources (base model/version where possible, question, DB, execution, time/token/tool/retry budgets, source knowledge, scorer); preserve intrinsic architecture. Document unavoidable model/tool asymmetry. Report paired deltas with CIs and McNemar tests; do not promote whichever contrast looks best. No full-context dump requirement for C2/C3; provide fair search/retrieval access.
Repeat/statistics decision: 3 sealed repetitions per condition = 1,212 frozen outputs. Sole primary endpoint: C4 run-1 accuracy on 101. Run-1 C1-C4 paired confirmatory contrasts; mechanistic C2-C1/C3-C2/C4-C3 use Holm correction for significance tests; C4-C1 overall contrast. Three-run analyses: per-run accuracy; per-question 3/3,2/3,1/3,0/3 correctness; correctness flips; no-answer/system failure; result-set agreement; latency/cost; question-clustered bootstrap CIs. Separate outcome reliability from result reliability; SQL variability diagnostic only. No voting/selection. Commit deterministic block-interleaved order over question x condition x repetition with repetitions separated; record timestamps/model IDs. All 1,212 generations complete before any gold scoring or result release. Normal evaluated-system retries are frozen; exhaustion counts incorrect/no-answer. Exogenous evaluator/DB/network failures may be rerun only under prespecified, logged criteria using the same trial identity; agent/harness failures are not infrastructure failures.
Information-tier decision: (1) public schema/HKB/questions available in development and runtime, frozen for test; (2) hidden train SQL/test cases/external_knowledge available only as offline supervision after pre-supervision baseline, never question-specific runtime inputs; (3) hidden test fields sealed-evaluator only. Preserve public-only mechanical HKB-to-Omni baseline before releasing train labels. Treat external_knowledge as privileged diagnostic oracle metadata: measure whether required nodes exist, dependencies compile, retrieval can reach them, and recurring classes fail; never use IDs to select runtime context. Gold-driven changes must be reusable system/model rules, not question-ID exceptions. Sample queries must encode reusable patterns, contain no benchmark question-to-gold pairs or IDs at runtime, have experiment/rationale/provenance/count, and receive an ablation if materially impactful. Final claim must acknowledge supervised development on 231 questions, not zero-shot.
Model-parity decision: C4 uses production-default Omni, unchanged except in-scope semantic-model/harness improvements. Inspect/record provider, observable model identifiers, tier(s), reasoning/token settings, retries, and stage-specific model use. Match C1-C3 exactly to C4 when independently invocable; otherwise pin one capable model across C1-C3. Production fidelity outranks forcing C4 parity. Predeclare interpretation before scoring: if exact parity, C4-C3 is an approximate controlled architectural contrast subject to remaining differences; if not, it is only a production-system comparison. C2-C1 and C3-C2 remain controlled within the matched direct-SQL system.

title: Report must state the token reduction as a bounded-payload claim, not a system-cost claim
description:
Tracking a framing commitment, so it is not lost between now and the write-up.

An external stakeholder has the figure "~100x fewer tokens via progressive
discovery / intelligent schema retrieval" from a progress email. As written that
is defensible and describes the retrieval payload. It is not defensible as a
statement about system cost.

What the evidence supports:
  inspect_schema returned the entire schema (51 tables, ~170K input tokens in the
  following turn) at commit 349e0bb. Since 2b72244 it returns at most 4 tables and
  64 KiB, enforced structurally. Two orders of magnitude, guaranteed by the bound
  rather than measured.

What it does NOT support:
  The 1,585-token / $0.017715 replay figure is an aborted attempt. It terminated
  at forbidden_tool_payload before any database query, and the research log
  records "end-to-end success remains unproven". It is 170K-before-failing versus
  1.6K-before-failing; neither run answered.

Ground truth from public-baseline-v1-direct-16db-continuation-1 (518 captures):
  median input tokens  c1 127,310  c2 198,968  c3 152,976
  mean cost            c1 $1.48    c2 $1.71    c3 $1.84
  turns per attempt    median 5, max 12
  largest single turn  median 61,892, p99 184,543
  attempts with any turn >=169,995: 12 of 518 (2.3%)
  model_budget_error: 17 of 518 (3.3%), down from deterministic on the canary

Requirement: the write-up states the bounded-payload claim with its bound, and
gives per-attempt cost separately, so the two cannot be conflated. Lead with the
precise version rather than presenting it as a retraction.
close_reason: Current results report cleanly separates the structural payload bound from system cost and preserves the aborted-diagnostic caveat.
